segments.say: Let your body settle where it is. Let your shoulders soften, and let your hands rest. For the next little while, there are no decisions to make. Nothing to choose, nothing to compare, nothing to calculate. Every choice can wait until tomorrow. Right now, there's only rest.

Take a slow breath in. And let it out, slowly. Again. In, gently. And out. Notice how your breath costs nothing. It asks for nothing. It simply comes and goes, all by itself, the way it has every night of your life.

Imagine you're sitting by a small campfire, beside a quiet lake. The fire crackles softly. Its warmth reaches your hands and your face. Above you, the sky is full of stars. Out on the water, a gentle mist drifts slowly by. There is nowhere you need to be.

Let the warmth of the fire move into your body. Into your hands. Up your arms. Into your shoulders. Let your shoulders drop, just a little. Let the warmth move down your back, into your hips, and down through your legs, all the way to your feet. Heavy. Warm. Calm.

If any thoughts about money come, about bills or plans or worries, that's alright. Imagine placing each one, gently, into a small wooden box beside you. You can close the lid. They'll be safe there. You can open it again tomorrow, in the daylight, if you need to. For now, the box is closed.

Imagine a small boat resting in a quiet harbor, tied safely to the dock. It doesn't need to sail anywhere tonight. Let yourself be like that boat for a while. Still. Settled. Unmoving. Valued just for being here, without having to do anything at all.

Breathe in slowly. And as you breathe out, let your jaw soften. Let your forehead smooth out. Let the small muscles around your eyes relax. Let your tongue rest gently in your mouth. Each breath out, a little softer than the last.

The fire is burning lower now, glowing softly. The lake is perfectly still. The stars are bright and patient. They've been shining for longer than any coin or note has existed. They don't need anything from you. They're simply there, keeping quiet company with the night.

Let's travel slowly through the body once more. Your feet, heavy and warm. Your calves, loose. Your knees, soft. Your thighs, sinking a little deeper. Your hips, settled. Your belly, rising and falling with each slow breath.
Your chest, open and calm. Your shoulders, heavy. Your arms, relaxed. Your hands, warm and still. Your neck, easy. Your face, peaceful. Your whole body, resting, supported, safe.

Think of something small and good that's waiting for you in the days ahead. Not something expensive. Something simple. A walk. A cup of coffee in the morning light. A conversation with someone you like. Let yourself feel a little warmth about it. And then let it rest too. It will be there when it's time.
The night is long and kind. It will carry you gently toward morning, while your body rests and your mind quietly sorts the day. You can trust the night. You don't need to hold onto anything.

Imagine the mist on the lake slowly rising, drifting over the water, soft and silver in the starlight. Let your thoughts drift with it, slowly, without direction. There's no destination. Nothing to reach. Just drifting.
Breathe in. And out. Slowly. The fire glows. The water is still. The stars shine. And you are resting, deeply, peacefully, letting go of the day, one breath at a time.

Everything that matters can wait for morning. Right now, you are safe, and warm, and completely at rest. Let sleep come to you, gently, in its own time, like the tide coming in on a calm, quiet night.
Softer. Quieter. Slower. There is nothing left to count, nothing left to plan. Only rest. Only the quiet night, holding you until morning.

Imagine walking slowly along a quiet path at night, beside the lake. The ground is soft under your feet. The air is cool and clean. With each step, you leave a little more of the day behind you. There's no hurry. The path will wait for you.

Somewhere in the distance, a night bird calls once, and then everything is quiet again. The water laps gently against the shore. In, and out. In, and out. Let your breathing follow that soft rhythm. Slow. Easy. Unhurried.

You come to a small wooden bench by the water. You sit down, and it feels exactly right. Your body grows heavier. Your hands rest in your lap. The stars reflect on the still surface of the lake, like scattered coins of silver light that no one needs to count.

Let your eyes feel heavy. Let your thoughts grow slower and softer, like the last embers of a fire. There is nothing you need to remember from tonight. Everything that mattered will still be there tomorrow, in the morning light.
Breathe in, gently. Hold it for just a moment. And let it go, long and slow. Once more. In. And out. Each breath carrying you a little further from the busy day, and a little closer to sleep.

You are safe. You are warm. You have done enough for today. Whatever you earned, whatever you spent, whatever you worried about, none of it needs your attention now. The night will hold it all, quietly, until morning.
Let yourself sink a little deeper. Into the bench, into the bed, into the quiet. Deeper. Softer. Calmer. The fire glows. The lake is still. And you are drifting, peacefully, toward sleep.

Picture a small temple garden at night, with cherry blossoms drifting slowly down in the lantern light. Each petal falls in its own time. None of them hurry. None of them worry about where they'll land. They simply let go, and float.

Let your thoughts be like those petals. Let them loosen, one by one, and drift slowly down, until they settle quietly on the ground. There's nothing to catch. Nothing to hold. Just the gentle falling, and the stillness after.
Your breathing is slow now. Your body is heavy and warm. The night is quiet all around you. Rest here, as long as you like. There's nowhere else you need to be.

And if you're still awake, that's perfectly fine too. Resting quietly in the dark is good for you, all by itself. Let the stillness be enough. Let this moment be enough. You are enough, exactly as you are, tonight.

Imagine the harbor again. The small boats rest quietly at their moorings. Their ropes creak softly as the water moves beneath them. A lantern on the dock glows warm and steady. There's no wind tonight. Only stillness, and the gentlest rocking of the sea.

Each boat is tied safely. None of them needs to go anywhere. They're simply resting, the way you're resting now. Held, steady, safe. Let your body feel like one of those boats. Gently rocking. Securely held.

If your mind drifts toward a decision you need to make, imagine writing it on a small piece of paper, folding it, and placing it in a lantern by the door. It will glow there, safe, until morning. You can come back to it when the sun is up. Not now.

Breathe in, slowly, like the tide coming in. And breathe out, even more slowly, like the tide going out. In. And out. The sea has been breathing like this for millions of years, never in a hurry. You can breathe with it.
Your arms are heavy. Your legs are heavy. Your eyelids are heavy. Each breath carries you a little further from the shore of the day, out onto calm, quiet water, under a sky full of patient stars.
There is nothing to choose. Nothing to compare. Nothing to get right. In sleep, everyone is equal, and everyone is safe. Let go of the day, and let the night carry you, gently, until morning.
Next time, we'll explore debt. How it works, why it can feel so heavy, and how people find their way out of it, calmly. But that's for another night. For now, rest well. Goodnight.
